scenes.tts: Chapter one treated each cluster as a candidate type. But can the same sensory neuron leave its cluster and later return? Follow its identity through development, injury and another species.
scenes.visual: Reuse chapter one’s exact colour map: type blue, RNA teal, genetic label gold, physiology green, injury red, uncertainty grey. Start on the carried schematic tree. One gold-outlined blue neuron leaves its branch toward a red island, then pauses beneath a question mark. Keep the tree moving gently.
scenes.narration: Chapter one treated each cluster as a candidate type. But can the same sensory neuron leave its cluster and later return? Follow its identity through development, injury and another species.

scenes.visual: Transform the question mark into the title ‘When Identity Changes’. Keep the tree and travelling neuron visible behind it.

scenes.tts: Mouse sensory neurons begin subtype specialization after they have become neurons. Early cells coexpress several transcription factors. The cells are not blank; specialization here refers only to subtype identity. Over development, those teal badges narrow into subtype restricted combinations. The broad starting population resolves into distinct blue branches.

The broad starting population resolves into distinct blue branches.
scenes.visual: Move a large developmental time slider. Gold-outlined post-mitotic neuron cartoons begin on one broad blue trunk, each carrying several teal TF badges. As the slider advances, badges fade selectively and cells glide into separate blue branches. Label the trajectory ‘mouse development, schematic’.
scenes.narration: Mouse sensory neurons begin subtype specialization after they have become neurons. Early cells coexpress several transcription factors. The cells are not blank; specialization here refers only to subtype identity. Over development, those teal badges narrow into subtype-restricted combinations. The broad starting population resolves into distinct blue branches.

scenes.tts: Signals from targets contribute to that narrowing. Removing nerve growth factor changed subtype restricted expression in mouse dorsal root ganglia. Fewer distinct populations remained when nerve growth factor was absent. Keeping the affected neurons alive separated altered identity from selective death. The signal contributes; it does not set every fate alone.

scenes.visual: Extend axons from the branching neurons to a large skin target. Teal ‘NGF’ arrows travel back along selected axons. Remove those arrows while a gold survival shield keeps the affected neurons available for comparison; branch-specific badge combinations become less distinct. Keep the displayed neuron count fixed as a schematic of the controlled comparison.

scenes.tts: Now cut the peripheral axons. Several blue types lose their subtype markers and gather in one red Atf3 rich cluster. Is that cluster a new permanent type, or a shared state?
scenes.caption: Now cut the peripheral axons. Several blue types lose their subtype markers and gather in one red Atf3-rich cluster. Is that cluster a new permanent type, or a shared state?
scenes.visual: A cut appears across the peripheral axons. Blue branch colours fade under a red overlay as gold-outlined neurons move into one red island marked ‘Atf3-rich’. Show two answer doors: ‘new type’ and ‘shared state’.
scenes.narration: Now cut the peripheral axons. Several blue types lose their subtype markers and gather in one red Atf3-rich cluster. Is that cluster a new permanent type, or a shared state?

scenes.visual: Hold both answer doors and the question. Keep the red overlay breathing slowly, but do not open either door.

scenes.tts: It behaves as a shared injury state. Existing neurons from many subtypes enter it. The red program promotes regeneration while suppressing the usual subtype signatures. As axons regrow over time, subtype expression reappears and the neurons separate toward their earlier branches. Their fixed gold outlines reveal continuity beneath the changing RNA.
scenes.visual: Open the ‘shared state’ door. Move a recovery time slider while the cut axons extend toward skin. Red overlays fade and the same gold-outlined neurons travel back toward their original blue branches. Never create replacement neurons. Label the motion ‘schematic trajectory’.
scenes.narration: It behaves as a shared injury state. Existing neurons from many subtypes enter it. The red program promotes regeneration while suppressing the usual subtype signatures. As axons regrow over time, subtype expression reappears and the neurons separate toward their earlier branches. Their fixed gold outlines reveal continuity beneath the changing RNA.

scenes.tts: The timing is associated with target reinnervation, but timing alone cannot prove cause. Tracing injured neurons argues against selective death. It still does not show that contact with the target restores identity. Keep the causal arrow dashed.
scenes.visual: Draw a dashed grey arrow from ‘axon regrowth’ to ‘identity returns’, then place a question mark on it. A gold label reads ‘reporter-positive share unchanged’ above a timeline marked ‘1 week → 2 months’. Transform a crossed-out ‘selective death’ card into the words ‘argues against’, not ‘proves’.
scenes.narration: The timing is associated with target reinnervation, but timing alone cannot prove cause. Tracing injured neurons argues against selective death. It still does not show that contact with the target restores identity. Keep the causal arrow dashed.

scenes.tts: Species adds another boundary. In mouse, Tafa4 is mainly associated with one blue C fibre touch branch. In human tissue, TAFA4 was strongest in an A delta touch population. It also appeared in cold sensing and C fibre touch populations. The same marker does not guarantee the same type.
scenes.caption: Species adds another boundary. In mouse, Tafa4 is mainly associated with one blue C-fibre touch branch. In human tissue, TAFA4 was strongest in an Aδ touch population. It also appeared in cold-sensing and C-fibre touch populations. The same marker does not guarantee the same type.
scenes.visual: Split the carried tree into mouse and human halves. Show the largest mouse TAFA4 badge on the C-LTMR branch. On the human half, put the largest badge on the Aδ-LTMR branch and smaller badges on the cold-sensing and C-LTMR branches. Keep the branches blue and label the comparison ‘expression, not function’.
scenes.narration: Species adds another boundary. In mouse, Tafa4 is mainly associated with one blue C-fibre touch branch. In human tissue, TAFA4 was strongest in an Aδ touch population. It also appeared in cold-sensing and C-fibre touch populations. The same marker does not guarantee the same type.

scenes.tts: A missing cross species match may also come from method. Whole cells and nuclei capture different RNA. A missing group can reflect what the preparation captures, not biological absence. Integration methods are built to align data sets and can merge real differences. Match preparations, validate markers in tissue and seek independent function.

scenes.visual: Bring back chapter one’s preparation filter between mouse and human trees. Switch it from ‘whole cell’ to ‘nucleus’, making selected teal badges fade. Then show an integration clasp pulling nearby branches together. Three checks lock into place: matched method, tissue validation, independent function.

scenes.tts: An atlas is a snapshot of cells, methods and conditions. Follow cells through time before calling a cluster permanent. Cross species boundaries only after matching the view. Identity is biological, but every atlas samples it.
scenes.visual: Zoom out to a four-frame strip of the same gold-outlined neuron: developing, adult, injured and recovered. Place mouse and human method filters beneath the strip. A camera shutter closes around one frame, then reopens to show the full sequence.
scenes.narration: An atlas is a snapshot of cells, methods and conditions. Follow cells through time before calling a cluster permanent. Cross species boundaries only after matching the view. Identity is biological, but every atlas samples it.

scenes.visual: End card over the full carried tree and timeline. Large line: ‘Read every atlas with its resolution, state, method and species.’ Keep the gold-outlined neuron moving slowly along its branch.
